chunks: 19 - Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ṣafwān, from Al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Razīn, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two of them, peace be upon them:
Concerning a man who touched a carcass: is ghusl obligatory upon him? He said: “No; that only applies in the case of a human being.”

key_terms.الْإِنْسَانِ: the human being, specifying the case in which this ruling applies
key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: ritual bath required for specific causes
key_terms.مَيْتَةً: a carcass or dead creature not referring here to a human corpse

ai.seo_question: Is ghusl required after touching a dead animal or carcass in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about ritual purity after touching a dead body. It states that ghusl is not required for touching a carcass, and that this ruling applies specifically to a human corpse.
